title: Lettre Tate (mai 66) (Cristaux) : lettre (1966), tapuscrit (s.d.), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: section 1.13 of the May 1966 letter to Tate on crystals, Example 2, where S is smooth over a perfect field k of characteristic p. The previous page reduced crystals on S relative to W to compatible systems of crystals relative to W_n = W/p^{n+1}, and allowed localisation on S.

Steps on this page:
(1) Lifting. With S smooth and affine, choose smooth lifts S_n over W_n, compatible in n (S_n ×_{W_n} W_{n-1} = S_{n-1}). Such lifts exist and are unique up to non-unique isomorphism, by the vanishing of H^1 and H^2 with coefficients in the tangent sheaf on an affine scheme.
(2) Nilpotent invariance. Since S = S_0 → S_n is a closed immersion with nilpotent ideal, restriction from crystals on S_n to crystals on S_0 (over any base, here W_n) is an equivalence. This is the topological invariance of the infinitesimal or crystalline site under nilpotent thickenings.
(3) Description by stratifications. Since S_n is smooth over W_n, by 1.8 crystals on S_n relative to W_n are the objects on S_n with a stratification relative to Spec W_n, i.e. descent data on the formal completion of the diagonal of S_n ×_{W_n} S_n. So a crystal M on S is a compatible system (M_n) of stratified objects on the S_n.
(4) Global proper lift. Suppose S lifts to a scheme X proper (and smooth) over R = Spec W. The formal GAGA/comparison theorems (EGA III 4–5, the existence theorem) algebraize compatible systems of coherent modules and their stratification maps. Hence coherent crystals on S are equivalent to coherent O_X-modules with a stratification relative to W. A posteriori this category is independent of the chosen lift X.
(5) Generic fibre. Passing to X_K, which is proper and smooth over K = Frac W of characteristic 0, gives a 'restriction/localisation' functor from coherent crystals on S to coherent stratified modules on X_K.
(6) Local freeness and connections. A coherent stratified module on a scheme locally of finite type over a field is locally free. In characteristic 0 on smooth X_K, a stratification is the same as an integrable connection. The next page continues: Riemann–Hilbert over C, triviality when π_1 = 1, and the isocrystal functor being fully faithful but not essentially surjective.

Purpose: relate crystals in characteristic p to characteristic-0 objects (de Rham theory, integrable connections), as a route to a 'transcendental' approach to families of Dieudonné modules and formal groups.
errors: 'stratifiés relativement à X_K' should read 'relativement à K' (Spec K): stratification of a module on X_K is taken relative to the base field.

Step (4) tacitly needs X smooth over W (properness alone is stated), so that the generic fibre is smooth and stratification relative to W is the right notion. The text later says X_K is 'propre et lisse', so smoothness is implicitly assumed.

The local freeness claim for stratified coherent modules is stated without proof ('on voit facilement'). It is correct (crystals on the infinitesimal site are locally free when the base is a field), but only sketched.

ideas.what: Crystals on S relative to W_n equal crystals on a smooth lift S_n (nilpotent invariance), hence stratified modules on S_n
ideas.modern_name: Topological invariance of the crystalline/infinitesimal site; crystals as modules with (HPD-)stratification
ideas.where_published: Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes (Dix exposés, 1968)

ideas.what: For a proper lift X/W, coherent crystals on S are equivalent to coherent O_X-modules with stratification relative to W, via formal GAGA; independent of the lift
ideas.modern_name: Algebraization of crystals/F-crystals via Grothendieck existence theorem
ideas.where_published: Letter to Tate (1966, widely circulated); ideas in Dix exposés

ideas.what: Functor from (iso)crystals on S to modules with integrable connection on the generic fibre X_K
ideas.modern_name: Realization of convergent isocrystals as connections on the generic fibre (rigid analytic tube)

ideas.what: Coherent stratified modules on a scheme locally of finite type over a field are locally free
ideas.modern_name: Local freeness of coherent crystals / coherent D-modules that are O-coherent
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore (Grothendieck; Katz; Gieseker in char p)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a page of the well-known 1966 letter to Tate, whose content was absorbed into Dix exposés, Berthelot's crystalline cohomology, and Ogus's convergent isocrystals. Nothing here is absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: 'Comme S_n b est lisse' : the 'b' is a stray typing artifact; read 'Comme S_n est lisse'.
'stratifiés relativement à X_K' is as typed but mathematically should be 'relativement à K'.
'un[-feur-] système' : struck text is likely 'peur'/'pour', irrelevant.
Insertion above 'relativement' reads 'sur S_n', correctly captured.
Insertion 'M' above 'cristal' (un cristal M sur S) is correct.
